headline_marked: 349 lawmakers vote as [[presidential election voting begins]] in Jatiya Sangsad
headline: 349 lawmakers vote as presidential election voting begins in Jatiya Sangsad
summary: Lawmakers cast ballots for candidates Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Col (retd) Oli Ahmed following the resignation of President Mohammed Shahabuddin.
details: The presidential polling began this afternoon at the Jatiya Sangsad, where 349 lawmakers are expected to cast their votes for candidates Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Col (retd) Oli Ahmed.
Acting President Hafizuddin Ahmed, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, and other high-ranking officials including the Chief Whip and opposition leaders have already cast their ballots.
Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin explained the voting procedure and informed lawmakers that counting will begin after 5:00 PM.
The election is being held following the resignation of President Mohammed Shahabuddin on July 24, with the winner to be declared on a preliminary basis inside the chamber.
Under the 1991 Presidential Election Act, the president is elected by members of parliament, and the entire process including counting is being telecast live on BTV.
caption:
349 lawmakers are casting their ballots today to elect the next President of Bangladesh.

The presidential polling began this afternoon at the Jatiya Sangsad, where 349 lawmakers are expected to cast their votes for candidates Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Col (retd) Oli Ahmed.

Acting President Hafizuddin Ahmed, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, and other high-ranking officials including the Chief Whip and opposition leaders have already cast their ballots.

Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin explained the voting procedure and informed lawmakers that counting will begin after 5:00 PM.

The election is being held following the resignation of President Mohammed Shahabuddin on July 24, with the winner to be declared on a preliminary basis inside the chamber.

Under the 1991 Presidential Election Act, the president is elected by members of parliament, and the entire process including counting is being telecast live on BTV.

Source: Somoy News, Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Nahid Islam claims [[Presidential election is partisan]] with no room for free voting
headline: Nahid Islam claims Presidential election is partisan with no room for free voting
summary: The opposition Chief Whip alleges the Prime Minister is hand-picking the President, calling the process a continuation of 'autocratic' constitutional systems.
details: National Parliament opposition Chief Whip and NCP convener Nahid Islam criticized the presidential election process, stating that the lack of free voting opportunities makes the office less honorable.
caption:
Is the presidential election just a formality? Nahid Islam claims the Prime Minister is hand-picking the winner while MPs have no real choice.

National Parliament opposition Chief Whip and NCP convener Nahid Islam criticized the presidential election process, stating that the lack of free voting opportunities makes the office less honorable.
